s:
Consider the following statements regarding the opening of the Constituent Assembly:
1. The first meeting was attended by 211 members.
2. The Muslim League boycotted the first meeting.
3. Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected President at the first meeting itself.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The first meeting was attended by 211 members, while the Muslim League boycotted it. Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected President on 11 December 1946, not at the first meeting.
tq: Find the incorrect statement by checking the precise sequence of events and dates.
sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Publication of the Draft Constitution
B. Adoption of the Objectives Resolution
C. Beginning of the third reading of the Constitution
D. Setting up of the Drafting Committee
x: The Objectives Resolution was adopted on 22 January 1947, the Drafting Committee was set up on 29 August 1947, the Draft Constitution was published on 21 February 1948, and the third reading began on 14 November 1949.
tq: Place the earliest dated event first and then verify the middle sequence.
sec: Sessions and dates - first meeting, Objectives Resolution, adoption, signing, final session, time taken

1. Draft Constitution published

It held 11 sessions and sat for 165 days over 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.

The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly in 1946

s:

A. Acceptance of the demand in principle in the August Offer
B. Cabinet Mission scheme
C. Tilak's Swaraj Bill
D. The demand becoming an official Congress demand
x: Tilak's Swaraj Bill belongs to 1895, the Congress adopted the demand in 1935, the August Offer accepted it in principle in 1940, and the Cabinet Mission scheme followed in 1946.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the role of the Cripps Proposals in relation to the Constituent Assembly?
o: They introduced the Indian Independence Bill in the House of Commons.
They provided for the election of all members by adult franchise.
They carried forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly after its acceptance in principle in the August Offer.
They finally constituted the Assembly through the Cabinet Mission Plan.
x: The Cripps Proposals of 1942 carried forward the proposal after the British had accepted the demand in principle through the August Offer of 1940. The Assembly was ultimately formed under the Cabinet Mission scheme in 1946.
tq: Distinguish between an intermediate proposal and the plan that actually constituted the Assembly.
sec: Idea of a Constituent Assembly - first proposer, Congress demand, British acceptance  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Independence Act, 1947:
1. It received royal assent on 18 July 1947.
2. It came into effect on 15 August 1947.
3. It provided for the creation of two dominions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The Act received royal assent on 18 July 1947, created the two dominions, and took effect on 15 August 1947.
tq: Check each statement against the sequence of assent, provisions and commencement.

s: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 provided that the two new dominions would have the right to:
o: remain permanently under the British Parliament
retain the office of the Viceroy permanently
x: The Act created two dominions with the right to secede from the Commonwealth. It did not permanently retain British legislative supremacy or the office of the Viceroy.
tq: Test the precise constitutional status granted to the new dominions rather than a general idea of independence.

s: Which of the following correctly describes India's status on 15 August 1947?
o: A sovereign republic with no constitutional link to the Crown
A federation of independent princely states
A Dominion with the British monarch as nominal head
A colony governed directly by the British Parliament

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Governor-General after independence:
1. The same Governor-General could, in principle, be appointed for both Dominions.
2. Each Dominion could have its own Governor-General.
3. The Governor-General was to act on the advice of the Dominion ministers.

x: All three statements are correct. The arrangement permitted one common Governor-General or separate Governors-General, who were to act on ministerial advice.

s:

B. Lord Mountbatten became Governor-General of free India
C. C. Rajagopalachari became Governor-General
D. India became a Dominion
x: Mountbatten became Governor-General in 1947, India became a Dominion on 15 August 1947, Rajagopalachari assumed office in June 1948, and India became a Republic on 26 January 1950.
tq: Fix the first and last events before ordering the middle events.

s: Dominion status of India ended when India became a Republic on:

s:
With reference to the partition procedure under the Mountbatten Plan, consider the following statements:
1. The Punjab and Bengal Assemblies met in separate sections representing Muslim-majority and Hindu-majority districts.
2. A simple majority in either section was sufficient for partition of the province.
3. Both Punjab and Bengal voted for partition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The two provincial Assemblies met in separate sections, and a simple majority in either section led to partition; both provinces voted for partition.
tq: Test the voting mechanism and its result together.

o: It resulted in the province joining India after a Congress-led campaign.
It was replaced by a vote of the Bengal Assembly.
It resulted in the province becoming an independent state.

fix the boundaries between the new Dominions

s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Indian Independence Act, 1947?
o: Lapse of British paramountcy over princely states
Continuation of the office of the Viceroy as the constitutional head of both Dominions
Abolition of the office of the Secretary of State for India
Creation of two Dominions, India and Pakistan

continue British paramountcy over princely states

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Constituent Assemblies under the Indian Independence Act, 1947:

2. They could repeal any British law, including the Indian Independence Act itself.
3. They were required to retain all British laws permanently.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Constituent Assemblies had sovereign constitutional authority; they were not required to retain British laws permanently.
tq: Spot the absolute reversal in the statement containing “permanently”.

s: Until a new Constitution was framed, each Dominion was governed under the:

Government of India Act, 1919, without alteration

o: The Crown retained a veto over Dominion bills and retained the title Emperor of India.
The Crown became the elected head of both Dominions.
The Crown retained paramountcy over princely states but lost control over civil services.
The Crown lost its veto over Dominion bills and the title Emperor of India was dropped.

The Constituent Assembly was barred from altering civil-service arrangements.

British suzerainty over the princely states ended.

s: After the Indian Independence Act, 1947, the Constituent Assembly performed which of the following functions?
o: It functioned only as the provincial legislature of the newly formed Union
It functioned as the legislature of British India under the control of the Viceroy
It functioned only as the constitution-making body until 26 January 1950
It functioned both as a sovereign constitution-making body and as the Dominion legislature
x: The Act made the Constituent Assembly fully sovereign in its constitution-making role and also made it the Dominion legislature. The Central Legislative Assembly consequently ceased to function.
tq: Distinguish the Assembly’s dual constitutional and legislative roles.

Dr B.R. Ambedkar and G.V. Mavalankar
Jawaharlal Nehru and Dr Rajendra Prasad
Dr Rajendra Prasad and G.V. Mavalankar
x: Dr Rajendra Prasad chaired the Assembly in its constitution-making capacity, whereas G.V. Mavalankar presided over it when it functioned as the legislature.

the British Government dissolved the provincial representation

Consider the following statements regarding the Radcliffe Boundary Commissions:

x: The award was ready on 12 August 1947 but was published on 17 August 1947. The delayed publication was intended to avoid Britain being blamed for the violence associated with partition.

o: 3 years, 1 month and 18 days; 12 sessions and 175 sitting days
2 years, 9 months and 18 days; 10 sessions and 160 sitting days
2 years, 11 months and 18 days; 11 sessions and 165 sitting days

s:
Consider the following statements about the preparation of the Indian Constitution:
1. The framers consulted the constitutions of about 60 countries.
2. Approximately Rs 64 lakh was spent on the constitution-making process.
3. The Draft Constitution initially contained 395 Articles.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The framers consulted the constitutions of about 60 countries and the expenditure was about Rs 64 lakh. The Draft contained 315 Articles; 395 Articles belonged to the adopted text, so statement 3 is false.
tq: Use the wrong-stage numerical trap involving the Draft and the adopted Constitution.

o: The Draft had 395 Articles, whereas the adopted text had 315 Articles.
The Draft had 315 Articles and the adopted text had 470 Articles.
The Draft had 315 Articles, whereas the adopted text had 395 Articles.
Both the Draft and the adopted text had 395 Articles.
x: The Draft Constitution contained 315 Articles. The Constitution as adopted contained 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.
tq: Compare figures belonging to successive versions instead of treating them as interchangeable.
